items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Topics 18:1
items.html: In the three names in the Mocha Stima'ah there are two changes on the three of the Galgalta: one, in the Tzere that is transformed into a Segol, which indicates a coupling of HB and the illumination of Hochma, as above; this was not in the Galgalta, and therefore their Heys are vocalized with a Tzere, whereas here, where the illumination of Hochma operates, their points are with a Segol. And the second change is that the Kamatzim that are in the three names of the Mocha deAvira are here transformed into Patachin. And it is for the aforementioned reason, that Kamatz is the aspect of Keter and Patach is the aspect of Hochma; and therefore the Kamatzim in the Mocha deAvira, which indicate the aspect of Keter, are here transformed into Patachin, into the aspect of Hochma. (Vol. 1, p. 316, Item 47).
